t: Truganini, a member of the Nuenonne people, saw her mother murdered by sailors and two of her sisters kidnapped by a sealer, and in her teens and twenties lived through the Black War between colonists and Aboriginal Tasmanians.

From 1830 she guided George Augustus Robinson on expeditions that ended in the exile of the Aboriginal people of the Tasmanian mainland, and she was herself exiled to Wybalenna on Flinders Island in 1835.

After her death the colonial government declared the island's Aboriginal population extinct, a claim scholars and the Aboriginal Tasmanian community reject, and her remains were displayed for decades against her wishes before being cremated and scattered in 1976.
dyk: Truganini twice saved Robinson's life by swimming across the Arthur River with him or towing his raft, in 1832 and 1834, yet she begged her doctor that her body not be mutilated by scientists after her death.
ev: Truganini is born at Recherche Bay, the youngest daughter of Manganerer of the Nuenonne
Robinson brings her to his mission at Missionary Bay on Bruny Island, and in October she marries Woureddy
She sets out as a guide on Robinson's "friendly mission" to the Aboriginal peoples of western and north-western Tasmania
Robinson announces that the Aboriginal population of the Tasmanian mainland has been exiled, and Truganini is taken to Wybalenna on Flinders Island
She is tried at Melbourne with four others and acquitted as an accessory; Maulboyheenner and Peevay are convicted and hanged in January 1842
The survivors at Wybalenna, Truganini among them, are moved to Oyster Cove
Truganini dies in Hobart, and the Tasmanian government declares the island's Aboriginal population extinct
Her remains, held by the Tasmanian Museum, are cremated and scattered in the D'Entrecasteaux Channel

f.born: c. 1812 at Recherche Bay, southern Tasmania (then Van Diemen's Land), the youngest daughter of Manganerer, the senior man of the Nuenonne clan; her mother was likely a member of the Ninene people
f.died: 8 May 1876 in Hobart, in the Dandridge family home, after falling into a coma on 4 May; she had contracted bronchitis the year before
f.role: Nuenonne woman; guide to George Augustus Robinson on his expeditions of 1830 to 1836; resident of the Wybalenna Aboriginal Establishment and of Oyster Cove
f.known: growing up on Bruny Island during British colonisation; guiding Robinson's expeditions in the Black War; exile at Wybalenna; the trial of 1841 at Melbourne; the mistaken description of her as the last Aboriginal Tasmanian; the treatment of her remains and their cremation in 1976
